summary: Lake Champlain light at Whallon Bay near Essex: first lit 1838, limestone tower 1867, steel-tower light from 1928; private residence, closed.

corrections.why: The standing tower is 39 ft (12 m) and is the 1867 octagonal limestone tower (USLHS: tower established 1867, height 39 ft). The 1835 date traces to the first tower, which LighthouseFriends describes as 30 ft and lit in 1838.
USLHS lists the tower shape as OCTAGONAL; LighthouseFriends describes the 1867 tower as octagonal.

USLHS gives 1838 as the year established; LighthouseFriends says Congress appropriated funds on 3 March 1837 and the light first shone in 1838. The record's 1835 comes from Rowlett's directory and predates the appropriation.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1838 is the first light (USLHS; LighthouseFriends). The 1867 date is the standing limestone tower. Both sources are right about different structures.

1928 is the discontinuance of the station (USLHS) and the start of the steel-tower light (LighthouseFriends; 2001 newspaper). The 2003 date fits a move of the light off the steel tower back to the stone tower (LighthouseFriends). No single source states this reading.

notes_for_editor: Most of the 1837-1895 story, the 1875 wreck, the 1925 Beech incident, the 1931 sale, the 1959 ownership, the 2003 relighting and the 2014 Coast Guard statement come from LighthouseFriends alone (secondary; facts only; its quotes of the 1874 Lighthouse Board report and the 2014 release were not checked against originals). Treat them as unverified in primary sources. Focal height disagreement: LighthouseFriends gives a focal plane of 110 feet above the lake; the USLHS record gives 100 feet above water. The story states both. The record's focal height of 28.3 m is not corrected here. Printed pages checked: 1893 item 1010 is on printed p. 64 (scan p. 71), confirmed on the page image, which also shows the item in the Third District list; 1899 item 20 is on printed p. 77 (scan p. 113), from the page header in the OCR; the 1915 pennant entry is printed p. 147 (PDF p. 3), the 1917 flag entry printed p. 250 (PDF p. 2), and the 1922 flag entry printed p. 218 (PDF p. 10), all from the PDF page headers. The 1922 OCR reads 'SpUt Rock, . Y.... .James Wakefield. jl' in the 3d district table; it is read as Split Rock, N.Y., the same 'Split Rock, N. Y.' line the 1915 and 1917 tables print. The 1893 OCR reads 'Split Rocky near Essex' and the page image reads 'Split Rock, Lake Champlain, New York'. The keeper roster is the USLHS roster (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson); role normalised to keeper per roster.py. Salary for Delance ($350) is from LighthouseFriends; roster.py --detail also gives $350 from the archive's own detail for him. Minnesota's Split Rock (Lake Superior, 1910 onward) appears in many corpus hits; none is used. The record's Wikidata 'built 1835' and Rowlett's 1835 are not supported by any primary source here. Not found: an NRHP listing for this station; the USCG Historian's page could not be read through the Internet Archive, so its Split Rock entry is not used. Newspapers: Chronicling America searches for the 1875 wreck and the 1895-1927 keeper items found no New York hits. Privacy: the present owners are not named (LighthouseFriends names a family and the 1931 buyer; the 2001 article names the owner, not repeated here). Access: closed, private; the story does not encourage landing or climbing.
